title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

Like Chaos weapons, the Abyss Greatsword scales with Humanity (up to 10). When fully upgraded, with 10 Humanity, and 40/40 in Strength and Dexterity, the Abyss Greatsword deals the most raw physical damage among all of the Greatsword class weapons, beaten only by ultra greatswords and Great Hammers/Axes in this regard. This damage difference is not significant and when factoring in that Abyss Greatsword cannot be buffed, other weapons are capable of vastly out performing this sword without putting points into two different casting stats.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet: If one does not meet the Intelligence and Faith requirements but still meet the required Strength and Dexterity, they will still be able to do full damage with the sword, but, will get a stagger animation that makes them immune to backstabs. This occurs because since the Intelligence and Faith requirements don't actually affect the damage output, but rather the Strength and Dexterity, they can completely disregard investing to get the Intelligence and Faith stats to 18. However, the drawback to this is that it will not allow one to do any follow ups, as once this sword makes contact, it will bounce off, stopping the user from doing anything for a few seconds.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Compared to its Greatsword of Artorias' true version, the Abyss Greatsword has a distinct moveset, lower stat requirements, weighs one unit less, has a heavily deteriorated appearance, and deals purely physical damage. The strong attacks are reminiscent of those performed by Artorias himself. Despite requiring 18 Faith and Intelligence, the Abyss Greatsword does not scale off of these parameters. This should discourage most builds from utilizing this weapon.

Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Kalameet is resistant to all elements including being resistant to lightning damage (Lightning damage is supposed be effective against dragons but this is not the case, probably because of his peculiar body, so it is best to avoid lightning weapons as well as offensive miracles such as Lightning Spear). Therefore, it is recommended that players use purely physical weapons.
With the proper timing, all of Kalameet's attacks can be avoided with fast rolling.
Strafing to Kalameet's left is generally safest, as it is harder for his often-used Head Strike to hit the player.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet

If you kill him without Gough's help, he will have a special Dialogue.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : The player first encounters Kalameet on the second stone bridge in Royal Wood.

Kalameet can be confronted opposite the Colosseum where Knight Artorias is fought. Beyond some Abyss Attack Dogs lies a ladder running parallel to a waterfall. Shortly after moving into the clearing, Kalameet will fly through the canyon and breathe black fire at the Chosen Undead. After this attack, speaking to Hawkeye Gough will convince him to shoot down Kalameet, so players can properly engage in battle on the ground. It is not necessary to be struck by the attack in order to receive Gough's help, only that Kalameet performs it.

It is possible to kill Kalameet without Gough's help. However, doing so will take an inordinately long time and a very large amount of arrows and the player will not receive any souls as a reward.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet: Regardless, the Dragon Knights, who wore armor forged from the scales of Kalameet and used weapons created from his tail, persisted, and at some point arrived in Drangleic and settled in the Dragon Shrine. The group of knights would also join the covenant of the Dragon Remnants, apostles who venerated the primordial creatures and desired the perpetuity of their existence, seeking their scales to rise above their limited human existence. This group used the Dragon Eyes to invade the space and time of other knights and challenged them to claim their dragon scales, rewarding the best among them with the stones infused with the powers of the dragons to try to achieve transformation, as well as with the ancient Black Dragon Greatsword forged from Kalameet's tail.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Although the
calamitous ring created with the eye of Kalameet had no useful power and was merely hazardous, the artifact was passed down for thousands of years as a symbol of dragon worship. Its most fervent adherents even became convinced that the task of preserving it had been bestowed upon them as a sacred duty.

Like many other artifacts and beings connected to the ancient dragons, the ring of Kalameet also ended up at Archdragon Peak, a place where the remnants of the men-serpents and the dragon worshippers had gathered to venerate the primordial beings and attempted to achieve their perfect shape using stones imbued with the power of everlasting dragons. The ring was thus kept in front of the statue of one of those who, in meditation, had managed to partially achieve the draconic transformation.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
The left side of the waterfall seems to have more spots with less fire hitboxes (a few spots only have one to block with whatever shield you have).
The spells Great Magic Shield and Great Magic Barrier could seriously help in this situation. Great Magic Shield would let you use shields with less stability than Havel's and a lighter weight. Only problem is any time you two hand the bow, Great Magic Shield will disenchant from your shield. Great Magic Barrier could help greatly to null out that residual 10% magic damage that no shield can block down to roughly 1.5-0.5% magic damage, though it has few casts and costs a lot of faith.
If you have it and are willing to swap weapons every time you block, the Moonlight Greatsword adds 40 points of magic defense when equipped (and out).

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although Kalameet was defeated and killed, a group of knights found his corpse and used his scales to create armor close to the appearance of the dragon, while they used his talons to craft shields and his tail to forge several legendary weapons. As the centuries passed, the Black Dragon was consigned to mere legend, according which he was defeated by a brave warrior in a magnificent battle and that it was his tail that was used to forge these legendary weapons. In the region of Drangleic the name of Kalameet has been long lost and, while the legend of the pale dragon is told in various locales even if each account is fragmentary, the Black Dragon is rarely mentioned; some even say that it is only an an embellishment adopted in later retellings of the story.

Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - theories

In addition, his flames deal both magic and physical damage just like abyssal sorceries and pyromancies.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : One of the most important things to note about Black Dragon Kalameet is that his "fire breath" is actually dark sorcery-based. It deals both magic and physical damage and deals high stability damage. As such, instead of fire defense, players should increase their physical and magic defense.
Blocking Kalameet's fire breath is ill-advised: the magic damage will strike through the shield, damaging the player. Weaker shields will cause the player to have their guard broken, taking more damage than what the player would have initially taken. Only greatshields should be used to block Kalameet's fire breath and only Havel's Greatshield can reliably block it. Other options include the Cleansing Greatshield and the Stone Greatshield, but these can sometimes have their guard broken if the player is not careful in managing their stamina.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Kalameet is a descendant of the primordial archdragons.

Due to the appearance of "Disparity" and Souls following the ignition of the First Flame that allowed the evolution of life, Kalameet was born with unique characteristics compared to the original archdragons. He possessed a single orange eye, an ability to produce a high frequency noise which made his captured targets twice as vulnerable to damage, and an obsidian hide that made him resistant not only to magic and fire like other dragons, but even lightning which was their primary weakness.

Thanks to his extraordinary strength, Kalameet survived the extermination of the Dragons by the Lords during the war and persevered throughout the Age of Fire. At some point, after Oolacile was corrupted by the Abyss of Manus, the dragon took up residence in the area, where not even the mighty warriors left in Anor Londo dared to provoke his ire.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Because the tail is almost always out of reach, it is recommended to use Halberds to cut it, as is with all tails.
As with most other boss tail weapons, obtaining the sword can be much easier with the help of a phantom.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - killing_without_gough_s_help 
 killing_without_gough_s_help : Full Havel's Armor or Stone Armor (high poise)
Shield with high Physical and Magic defense and high stability (Havel's Greatshield, Cleansing Greatshield, Stone Greatshield).
Gough's Greatbow (just to kill Kalameet) or Dragonslayer Greatbow (to get special dialogue) with Gough's Great Arrows.
Hawk Ring could help, but only to get farther back, since it just adds range. Better ring choices would be Leo (for counter thrust damage (untested if Kalameet's fire gets counter damage))/Spell Stoneplate (Magic Def if lacking)/Steel Protection (phys def if lacking)/Favor and Protection (Stamina)/Cloranthy (Stamina regen (for low stamina))/Havel's (for that weight you're carrying)/Wolf (if you really think you need max poise).
The left side of the waterfall seems to have more spots with less fire hitboxes (a few spots only have one to block with whatever shield you have).

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
If you have it and are willing to swap weapons every time you block, the Moonlight Greatsword adds 40 points of magic defense when equipped (and out).
Power Within would be a little risky for this fight, only good if you really know where to block from and know for sure you will only block one hit from Kalameet's fire, where you will have space to heal and keep yourself topped off.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet:
Black Dragon Kalameet -  Dark Souls - boss - obsidian_greatsword 
 obsidian_greatsword : Severing Kalameet's tail and obtaining the Obsidian Greatsword can often prove more challenging than the battle itself, as the dragon's tail is mostly out of reach throughout the fight. His tail has 540 health on Ng and 847 health on NG+.
The tail becomes vulnerable to attack after Kalameet performs his Tail Smash, which is triggered when player is positioned under the tip of his tail, or during the Close Range Flame, which is triggered when standing directly in front of him. Of these, the Tail Smash leaves the tail most vulnerable.
**It is recommended to use high damage attacks such as Great Combustion, Dark Bead, or weapon augmentations when performing this strategy, since it's unlikely to get more than 2 hits per opportunity.
Because the tail is almost always out of reach, it is recommended to use Halberds to cut it, as is with all tails.

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: His true relevance is revealed once the player discovers Black Dragon Kalameet's whereabouts. After meeting the beast at the gorge, who flys out of reach and breathes fire from up above, returning to Gough will have him ask about the encounter and if the dragon is causing the player trouble. Answering yes to his question, and then to the question after, will make the old knight assist with the hunt, taking up his bow to shoot the dragon out of the sky and forcing him to engage with the player on the ground for a proper battle. Despite this, Gough's involvment is not necessary to kill Kalameet, but beating him differently will result in a slower, more tedious process than just fighting him head on like every other boss beforehand.

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: Regardless of how Kalameet is defeated, Gough will reward the player with his personal greatbow, though he needs to be talked to for that to happen. The only way to obtain his set, however, is by slaying him, which can be done at any point. He'll drop the bow too if he hasn't gifted it already.

title: Dragon
snippet: Black Dragon Kalameet may be encountered as an optional boss in the Royal Wood area of Oolacile and is supposedly the last of the Ancient Dragons. After its defeat, the Black Dragon and its final battle would become mere legend, very rarely mentioned and considered by some to be embellishments of the tale of the Pale Dragon. However, proof of its existence would be left in the form of many items made from its body and passed down by Dragon Worshippers: the Calamity Ring, made from and enchanted by Kalameet's orange eye; the Black Dragon Armor, made from its scales; the strangely-shaped Black Dragon Shield, made from its talons, and several oddly-shaped weapons made from its tail, including a Greataxe, a Warpick, and a Greatsword, the last of which is still capable of releasing its mystical power when wielded with both hands, unleashing an explosion of the gold and black flames of Kalameet. Two other weapons are said to have been crafted from black dragon's tail, though it is unclear

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: He witnessed the fall of Oolacile caused by their arrogance and greed, as well as Artorias' failure to quell the Abyss and his demise at the hands of the Chosen Undead. Should the time traveling hero choose to engage the legendary Kalameet, a dragon so fierce not even Anor Londo dared to cross him, Gough could even be allowed one last hunt, firing an impressive shot in spite of his now limited vision, speaking to the true might of the legendary archer. Having done that, though, he'll give away his precious bow, officially leaving that life behind him.

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet:
Hawkeye Gough -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : In the English version, he pronounces his own name as gɔːf, rhyming with the word "cough".
Him relying only on sound to track down the player if made hostile is reminiscent of the [https://demonssouls.fandom.com/wiki/Old_Hero Old Hero] from *Demon's Souls*, an ancient blind swordsman who does the same in his fight.
If you happen to be patient enough to do so, you can kill Kalameet with a greatbow, Gough's or Dragonslayer. If you do so, Gough will say a special dialogue. There are specific spots where you only get hit once by Kalameet's fire, which makes this easier.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - hawkeye_gough 
 hawkeye_gough : Hawkeye Gough was the only Giant of the Four Knights, and the leader of the Dragonslayers, the archers that fought the Dragons in the Age of Ancients.

By the time the Chosen Undead meets him, Gough is blind. Upon their first encounter, he thanks the Chosen Undead for slaying Artorias, allowing the corrupted knight to die with his honor intact.

Despite being blind, Gough was still a great sharpshooter. He proves this by shooting Kalameet out of the sky, on the Chosen Undead's request. This allowed the Chosen Undead to fight the dragon on more equal footing, eventually leading to the latter's demise.

Despite his skill, there were archers that rivaled even Gough. One such individual was Pharis , which was especially impressive as Pharis was only human.

title: Gaping Dragon
snippet:
Below 50% health, the dragon gains a new attack (corroding acid), that can reduce item and weapon durability, and even cause the player's equipment to break if stayed in too long. It's important not to confuse this attack with the stomach slam (their animations start in a similar way).
The Gaping Dragon's tail can be cut off, rewarding the Dragon King Greataxe, and the tail swipe's range becomes extremely short, making the rest of the fight easier. If you are trying to get the axe, hit the middle (or end) of the tail; if you aim at the base of the tail (i.e., the "buttock" area) it's possible to kill the dragon before the tail itself has taken enough damage.
A player phantom can offer ranged support and distract the Gaping Dragon from the balcony, if they don't enter the fog gate.

title: Black Dragon Set
snippet: After the Black Dragon Set is equipped, using the Dragon Head Stone makes the player breathe Fire and using the Dragon Torso Stone releases a shockwave similar to Force, while also giving the player a damage buff for 5 seconds. Both of these actions drain stamina, but while the fire breath is exhausted in a continuous rate, the damage buff will empty a large portion of the player's stamina bar. The stamina cost is set, and as such; the stamina loss is more manageable with high Endurance.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak can be entered only after learning the Path of the Dragon gesture found upon a corpse of a Drakeblood Knight in the Consumed King's Garden; this faction of knights can be summoned in Archdragon Peak by the man serpents there. Drakeblood Knights worshiped the blood of dragons; and the red cloth decorating their armor is said to symbolize their yearning for blood.

In Archdragon Peak, the Calamity Ring is found, reportedly made from the orange eye of a calamitous dragon, the ring considered a symbol of dragon worship. This dragon was none other than Black Dragon Kalameet, said to be the last one of ancient dragons.

The Nameless King, known for once allying with ancient dragons, resides on Archdragon Peak. He is accompanied by a stormdrake, which he tamed and fought alongside him. Dragon Slayer Ornstein's weapon and armor can be found laying around the Nameless King's arena; he was said to have left his guard in Anor Londo cathedral to search for the Nameless King.

title: Gaping Dragon
snippet:
Locking on can make evading the Gaping Dragon's attacks harder, as it reduces the speed at which the player can move away from the boss.
The Gaping Dragon will become momentarily still after its charge attack; this time can be used to attack it safely. The charge always comes after a stomach slam, so use the slam as a signal to get close to its side/tail.
Hitting its head deals extra damage, but the head is only accessible right after a slam (and before a charge). More experienced players can shorten the fight considerably by hitting the head a couple of times right after the slam, and quickly getting out of the way before the charge starts. A hit to its head does approximately 3x as much damage as a hit to the body.

title: Black Dragon Shield
snippet:
Black Dragon Shield -  Dark Souls II - shield - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Black Dragon Shield is a very powerful all-around shield with strong elemental defenses, allowing it to reliably block almost all forms of damage. Its decent stability makes it useful for warding off most forms of physical attacks.

However, it is also only available as a random drop in the very last area in the main game, meaning that its utility will be very limited. As well, like all other Black Dragon equipment, it requires the use of Petrified Dragon Bone to upgrade. Finally, it is one of the heavier medium shields in the game, meaning that equipping it may negatively impact players' mobility and equipment options.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet:
It is possible to almost become immune to its fire attacks by achieving a 890 fire defense.

Summons may be targeted as they enter the fight, making it hard for the player to reliably summon two phantoms.

An excellent strategy to overcome this dragon is to head straight for the back feet. Once there, the best place to stay is right between the middle and inner toes, in such a situation, the dragon will use his stomp attack almost exclusively. When he stomps, simply sprint to the other foot and continue. It is possible for him to use his inner flame attack. But this is easily avoided by simply walking away from the foot in which you were perched.

title: Gaping Dragon
snippet:
Gaping Dragon -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Being a Dragon, it is very susceptible to Lightning.
Staying at the Gaping Dragon's side and attacking its legs, moving only when it begins to walk or fly, can result in an easy victory.
Ranged attacks can prove useful, especially while the boss is performing a forward charge.
Be sure to kill the Channeler located on the highest floor above the arena to prevent it from casting ranged attacks during the boss fight. It does not respawn.
As long as care is taken with positioning, there is no need to block or dodge during the fight, making two-handed weapons an excellent choice for melee attacks.
Locking on can make evading the Gaping Dragon's attacks harder, as it reduces the speed at which the player can move away from the boss.

snippet:

Upon unlocking the door, Gough will act as a merchant. He won't be too chatty, and his wares aren't anything special for the most part, but he will sell unique items of his making, such as two of his carvings and his great arrows.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet:
Ancient Dragon -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia

The Ancient Dragon has more HP than most other bosses.
In the announcement trailer, the Ancient Dragon has a third eye in the middle of the other two, similar to Kalameet and is also noticeably smaller than he is in-game. In the final version, however, this design appeared to have been cut.

title: Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon
snippet:
Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon -  Dark Souls II - boss - encounters 
 encounters : The player first encounters Sinh before reaching the first bonfire in Shulva, Sanctum City. The dragon's breath can be heard before spotting him. He will be resting over a rocky structure, getting close to it will make the dragon roar and fly away. A second encounter will happen on the bridge leading to the entrance to Dragon's Sanctum. Sinh will appear and blast the bridge with fireballs, killing the two Sanctum Soldiers (and possibly the player if they stand too close).

The third and final encounter will happen after entering the white fog in Dragon's Rest, where the boss fight takes place. Sinh will wake from its slumber, throw its fiery breath upwards, and attempt to body slam the player from its nest before properly starting the battle.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Usage of the Dragon Eye is limited to players who are members of the Path of the Dragon covenant.

Using the Dragon Eye causes the player's sign to appear in the worlds of other players, allowing them to summon the user to their world to duel. The player does not need to be in human form. However, the host must be in human form (reverse-hollowed), but does not need to possess a Dragon Scale (contrary to the in-game description), and the area boss does not need to be alive to interact with the summon sign; users of the dragon eye have no such restrictions as to where and when they can place their signs. Players can summon others that are within their soul level +/-(10+10%) of their level; for example, a level 100 player can be summoned by anyone between level 80 and 120.
